name: UCI Superconductivty Data (Hamidieh 2018)
description: Composition-based superconducting critical-temperature regression benchmark derived from the original NIMS SuperCon database.
count_display: 21,263 tabular instances, 81 input features plus critical temperature
count_scope: Rows in the UCI regression release; train.csv and unique_m.csv are two representations of the same 21,263 samples

sources.title: UCI Superconductivty Data
sources.evidence: Official page reports 21,263 instances, 81 features, a formula companion file, NIMS SuperCon parentage and CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: UCI dataset 464 official metadata
sources.evidence: Confirms instance/feature counts, 2018 release and dataset DOI 10.24432/C53P47.

sources.title: A data-driven statistical model for predicting the critical temperature of a superconductor
sources.evidence: Primary paper describes formula-derived features, preprocessing of NIMS SuperCon data and the regression scope.

caveats: Derived from NIMS SuperCon; not an independent experimental acquisition or an additive expansion of the original/MDR collection.
No periodic atomic coordinates are included; repeated compositions and sample variants need not be unique compounds.
The two CSV files contain the same sample cohort and must not be added together.
Elemental thermal-conductivity and similar descriptors are computed feature aggregates, not measured compound properties.
The original regression task concerns known superconductors and does not establish classification of superconductors versus nonsuperconductors.

name: NIST WebHTS / High Temperature Superconducting Materials Database (SRD 62)
description: Evaluated literature data for oxide superconductors, linking thermal, mechanical and superconducting properties with composition, processing and numeric structural descriptors.
version: Data content last updated 1996; provider metadata version 1.0.0 (2015)
count_scope: Historical SRD 62 corpus; no numeric total inferred from portal or search choices
license: NIST Standard Reference Data copyright; all rights reserved. Specific redistribution license not verified; see provider SRD terms.

sources.title: NIST SRD 62 official resource metadata
sources.evidence: Identifies WebHTS, DOI 10.18434/T4KP8J, public access, oxide-superconductor scope, evaluated properties and structural tables.

sources.title: NIST WebHTS search portal
sources.evidence: Portal explicitly states last data-content update 1996; query fields include structure type and chemical family.

sources.title: NIST SRD copyright and licensing statements
sources.evidence: Distinguishes copyrighted Standard Reference Data from other NIST employee works; no blanket public-domain assumption is warranted.

caveats: Provider page remains reachable; no end-of-service declaration was found, but the scientific data are historical (last content update 1996).
Public browsing is distinct from permission to redistribute the copyrighted SRD compilation.
Numeric structural tables do not establish a downloadable CIF/atomic-coordinate dataset.
IEEE lists the metadata route and legacy search portal separately; both point to the same SRD 62 corpus.

name: Organic Superconductor Database (OSD)
description: Quasi-two-dimensional crystalline organic conductors and superconductors with literature measurements, CSD-linked crystal structures and tight-binding electronic calculations.
count_display: 184 CSD crystal structures associated with 110 materials and 440 measured properties (2022 paper)
count_scope: Historical 2022 publication cohort; 184 structures are not 184 independently confirmed superconductors or a current portal-total assertion

sources.title: A Database for Crystalline Organic Conductors and Superconductors
sources.evidence: 2022 paper reports 110 materials, 184 CSD structures and 440 measured properties; describes manual measurements and tight-binding calculations.

sources.title: OSD official about page
sources.evidence: Confirms open public browsing, CSD-source CIFs, manually entered literature measurements and tight-binding electronic structures.

caveats: Includes organic conductors and other correlated electronic states as well as superconductors; not every material has superconducting Tc.
Underlying CIFs originate from CSD; public links/viewers do not establish unrestricted coordinate redistribution.
The 184-structure publication cohort overlaps CSD and can contain multiple structures for one material.
Dataset-wide reuse licensing was not found; the paper’s article license is not substituted for data licensing.
HTTP public pages were reachable in the direct retrieval; an HTTPS browser-tool request failed, so the observed HTTP route is retained.

name: Robinson HTS Wire Critical Current Database
description: Experimental critical-current characterizations of commercial HTS wire and film samples across temperature, field magnitude and field angle, with n-values and downloadable data.
count_display: 24 public wire/film-characterization datasets in Figshare collection v23
count_scope: Collection articles_count=24, independently matched by the 24-item public articles list; not the number of measurement points or unique superconducting compounds

sources.title: Robinson HTS collection metadata
sources.evidence: Public collection v23 declares 24 articles and a 2025-10-14 publication snapshot.

sources.title: Robinson HTS public collection articles
sources.evidence: Public list contains 24 characterization datasets, including commercial wires and a YBCO film.

sources.title: Robinson HTS database official documentation
sources.evidence: Describes complete Figshare datasets for particular samples, critical-current/n-value curves and CC BY 4.0 licensing.

caveats: Twenty-four counts characterized wire/film datasets; each contains many operating-condition measurements and is not a new bulk crystal.
Commercial product/sample variation matters; multiple products can share the same superconducting composition.
No atomic-coordinate structures are promised by the wire-performance dataset.
The web visualizer is JavaScript-dependent; the Figshare collection provides the archival data route.
